parsed.use_case: A payment or cash-handling service must determine the smallest number of available denominations that exactly totals a requested amount, with each denomination reusable. This also models minimizing the number of fixed-size units needed to cover a quantity.
system_examples: Cash register and payment systems — choose a minimum-count set of available denominations for exact change when denominations are configurable.
Packaging and inventory systems — represent an order quantity using the fewest available package sizes, or report that it cannot be represented exactly.
parsed.explanation: Dynamic programming evaluates the best coin count for each amount using smaller amounts, taking O(amount × number of denominations) time and O(amount) space, versus enumerating combinations, which can grow exponentially. This matters when denomination sets do not have a reliable greedy rule; the exact optimization is useful, though the classic formulation is also largely a teaching problem.
